answer: A practical defence is Scroll-velocity fingerprint while reading the challenge. It rests on the speed and pauses of a reader scrolling the challenge text, which gives every honest agent a basalt that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the tundra compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The inlet is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
